hints: Focus on what simple molecular really means, small separate molecules held together only by weak intermolecular forces.
Remember that $\text{C}_{60}$ is a closed ball of 60 carbons that exists as separate molecules, while graphene and graphite are endless giant layers.
Check which other substance also exists as small separate diatomic molecules with low melting point, then pair it with $\text{C}_{60}$.
walkthrough:
**Recall what simple molecular means**

Think small and separate. A simple molecular solid is made of distinct small molecules held to each other by weak van der Waals forces.

Rule to use:
$$\text{small discrete molecules + weak intermolecular forces = simple molecular}$$

**Sort the carbon forms**

$\text{C}_{60}$ fullerene is a ball-shaped molecule. Each ball is separate from the next, so it is simple molecular.

Graphene is a single giant sheet of joined carbons, and graphite is many such sheets stacked. Both go on forever with strong covalent bonds, so both are giant molecular.

**Sort iodine**

Iodine exists as separate $\text{I}_2$ molecules. They are only attracted by weak London forces, which is why iodine sublimes so easily. So iodine is simple molecular.

Conclusion: the only pair where both are simple molecular is $\text{C}_{60}$ and iodine.

options.A: C60 is simple molecular, but graphene is not. Graphene is a giant covalent sheet of carbon atoms joined in a continuous hexagonal network, not separate small molecules.
options.B: Both are simple molecular and this is correct. C60 exists as separate buckyball molecules and iodine exists as separate I2 molecules, each held to neighbours only by weak van der Waals forces.
options.C: Neither is simple molecular. Graphene is a giant covalent monolayer and graphite is giant covalent layers stacked together. Both have infinite covalent bonding, not discrete molecules.
options.D: Iodine is simple molecular, but graphite is not. Graphite is a giant covalent structure with strong covalent bonds within layers, so it has very high melting point unlike simple molecular solids.
